subject: Model upgrade caused throughput & error surge - urgent
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@crestfield.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout

Jordan —

We pushed the new model bundle (v4.1 + afterburner quant profile) to production at 05:20 PT this morning (can provide the manifest). Within ~20 minutes we started seeing a sharp increase in response times and a rising 5xx rate for our high-concurrency checkout path. Key metrics: p95 latency up from 410ms -> 1.7s, 5xx rate climbed from 0.02% -> 1.9%, overall throughput dropped ~18% for that route.

This is customer-impacting for our peak window. We opened a PagerDuty incident (link below) and are throttling requests on our side as a temporary measure, but we need Redwood to triage immediately. We attached a screenshot of the error spike and a short timeline.

Please advise rollback/mitigation steps and whether you can force a canary rollback of the afterburner profile. We will coordinate our side but need Redwood to lead the rollback if possible.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Crestfield Payments

Attachments: crestfield_error_screenshot-500.png, crestfield_timeline.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@crestfield.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout

Thanks Elena — and sorry for the disruption.

Short answer: we can schedule an immediate canary rollback for your scope and pull the afterburner quant profile out of the serving variants. To move fast I need: (1) confirmation of the model bundle id you deployed (or attach the manifest), (2) the exact route names where you see the regression, and (3) a link to the incident (you included pagerduty — we’ll watch it).

Internal note: Irene + Karthik — I’m asking for an emergency rollback of the afterburner profile for the Crestfield account. If we can flip the quant profile back to the previous stable variant and pin it, that should restore latency while we investigate. Also consider toggling batching/windowing to lower concurrency pressure.

Proposed immediate actions:
- We stage a rollback for 10:00 PT to be executed as a canary (10% traffic) and monitor p95, 5xx, and throughput for 30 minutes.
- If metrics improve, we roll back 100% and schedule postmortem.
- Offer a credit for the impacted window (Grace, need exec sign-off).

I’ll set up a quick bridge in 10m.

—Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@crestfield.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout

Looping in ops detail. Jordan — on our side we have two quick mitigations to try in parallel:

1) Revert the afterburner quant profile for the named model variants Crestfield is using (profile id: afb-20260319). This is low-risk and should be atomic.
2) If revert is insufficient, temporarily reduce max active batch size on the route and enable prefix KV caching for frequent requests (their checkout traffic benefits a lot from prefix reuse).

I’ve prepared a rollback manifest and a short-runbook (attached as afterburner_rollout_manifest.json) that maps the variant IDs to customer routes. If Jordan will run the canary, Karthik and I will monitor infra metrics and be on the bridge.

Irene
Sr. Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@crestfield.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout

Thanks — manifest attached (afterburner-rollout-manifest.json). We deployed to the following routes: /api/checkout/v1/price, /api/checkout/v1/verify. PagerDuty incident PDT-98234 is live.

Note: we already started a partial throttle on our side which reduced error volume but didn’t fix latency. If you start a canary rollback please alert us before flipping 10% -> 100%. I will be on the bridge and can pause downstream systems if needed.

Elena

Attachments: afterburner_rollout_manifest.json, crestfield_error_screenshot-500.png

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout — Exec attention requested

Grace — forwarding a live customer incident at Crestfield. They rolled our v4.1 afterburner quant profile this morning and are seeing a p95 and 5xx spike on high-value checkout routes. Engineering suggests immediate rollback of the quant profile as the primary mitigation.

Why I’m escalating: this hits their SLAs in a peak window and they’ve asked for prioritized support. They are an active commit account (DEAL-4732) with multiple production integrations. We should offer an immediate operational credit for the impacted window and confirm ownership on the rollback execution.

PagerDuty: https://company.pagerduty.com/incidents/PDT-98234
Runbook (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/eng/crestfield-logs-20260321

—Jordan
Account Executive

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@crestfield.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 10:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Performance spike after the v4.1-afterburner rollout — Exec attention requested

Thanks for the heads up and for moving quickly. Approve the immediate rollback plan described by Irene. Please execute the 10% canary at 10:50 PT and evaluate for 30 minutes. If p95 and 5xx reduce to within 10% of baseline, proceed to 100% rollback.

Authorization: offer Crestfield a 2-day service credit for the impacted window and escalate to our DX team to prioritize the postmortem. Jordan — please confirm the credit and follow up with the customer after the rollback.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
